newsitem.title: USA: California Microwave to cut jobs, close plants.
newsitem.headline: California Microwave to cut jobs, close plants.

text.p: California Microwave Inc. said Wednesday it will cut 20 percent of its staff and close facilities in California and Illinois by March 31 in a restructuring.
The supplier of satellite earth station and microwave radio infrastructure products did not specify how many jobs would be cut. Company officials were not immediately available to comment.

The company said it will take an $8 million charge to account for the actions in the third quarter ending March 31. The largest part of the charge involves writing off product warranty reserves at its Microwave Network Systems unit.
Separately, the company reported a net loss of $25.4 million, or $1.57 cents a share, for the second quarter ended Dec. 31, including an initial $39 million charge for its restructuring plans.
This compared with earnings of $3.6 million, or 23 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
Sales edged up to $117.1 million from $116.3 million.
California Microwave said the largest portion of the $39 million charge was taken to boost its two primary divisions.

Under the restructuring, California Microwave will refocus its Microwave Network unit on the equipment markets for personal communications service networks and cellular communications in developing countries.

Its second business division, Satellite Transmission Systems, will focus on its operations in systems integration and network configuration. Its satellite earth station products will be transferred to another division called EFData.
In December, Chief Executive Philip Otto resigned from the company, and in January Chief Financial Officer Dennis Raney decided to leave the company at the end of February.

The company has formed an executive committee headed by Chairman David Leeson to lead the company during its restructuring. George Spillane, currently vice president and secretary will assume Raney's duties when he departs.
California Microwave's stock rose 50 cents to $17.875 on Nasdaq.
